components.name: appbar
components.contract: reads app.name, app.page, app.user, app.env
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <!-- COPY: the app bar is a one-row `row` with class `k-appbar`. The
           class docks it to the top of its parent (`dock: top`), so the
           content below it keeps all the remaining space whatever it is.
           Put at most one top-docked bar in a container. -->
      <row class="k-appbar">
        <text class="k-appbar-brand">◆ {app.name}</text>
        <text class="k-appbar-title">{app.page}</text>
        <spacer/>
        <text class="k-appbar-meta">{app.user}</text>
        <text class="k-badge ok">{app.env}</text>
      </row>
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: statusbar
components.contract: reads status.mode, status.file, status.synced, status.position
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
      <!-- COPY: the status bar is a one-row `row` with class `k-statusbar`,
           docked to the bottom of its parent. Left segments first, a
           `spacer`, then right segments. `k-statusbar-seg` is a filled chip
           (modifiers: ok, warn, danger); `k-statusbar-text` and
           `k-statusbar-muted` are plain. Only one bottom-docked bar per
           container (L005): put the key hints above it, not docked. -->
      <row class="k-statusbar">
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg">{status.mode}</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-text">{status.file}</text>
        <spacer/>
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg ok" if="status.synced">synced</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-seg warn" if="!status.synced">unsynced</text>
        <text class="k-statusbar-muted">{status.position}</text>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: breadcrumb
components.contract: reads crumbs[] {id, label, last}, where; the host trims crumbs on breadcrumb_up
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="backspace" action="breadcrumb_up" label="up"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1">
      <!-- COPY: a breadcrumb is a `row` with class `k-breadcrumb` and `each`
           over an array of {id, label, last}. Its children are the template,
           repeated per element: the label (class `k-breadcrumb-item`, plus
           `current` for the last one, by a class:NAME guard) and the
           separator. The host builds the array from the current path and
           trims it on `breadcrumb_up`. A template cannot hold anything
           focusable, so the crumbs are display only; navigate with a keymap
           row. -->
      <row class="k-breadcrumb" each="crumbs as c" key="c.id">
        <text class="k-breadcrumb-item" class:current="c.last">{c.label}</text>
        <text class="k-breadcrumb-sep" if="!c.last">›</text>
      </row>
      <text class="k-muted" pad="1">You are in {where}.</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: tabs
components.contract: reads and writes view (the active tab's id); reads tabs.overview, tabs.activity, tabs.settings, tabs.count
components.actions: none (the keymap uses the built-ins move-next, move-prev, switch-to)
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="]" action="move-next" to="#nav" keycap="]/[" label="tab"/>
    <bind keys="[" action="move-prev" to="#nav"/>
    <bind keys="1" action="switch-to" to="#overview"/>
    <bind keys="2" action="switch-to" to="#activity"/>
    <bind keys="3" action="switch-to" to="#settings"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0">
      <!-- COPY: tabs are a `tabs` with class `k-tabs` bound to a path that
           holds the active tab's id (the host or `switch-to` writes it).
           Write `focusable` on it: whether a tab strip takes focus is then
           your choice, not a default. Each `tab` needs an `id` (yours, not
           a kit part: it is the value of the bound path) and a `label`;
           `short` is the label used when the strip does not fit. The
           generated labels are styled by the class (`.k-tabs > .tab-label`).
           Only the active tab's content is laid out. `mark` is the glyph
           before the active label. -->
      <tabs id="nav" class="k-tabs" bind="view" mark="▸" focusable="true">
        <tab id="overview" label="1 overview" short="1 ovr">
          <box class="k-card" title="Overview">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.overview}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
        <tab id="activity" label="2 activity ({tabs.count})" short="2 act">
          <box class="k-card" title="Activity">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.activity}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
        <tab id="settings" label="3 settings" short="3 set">
          <box class="k-card" title="Settings">
            <text class="k-card-text">{tabs.settings}</text>
          </box>
        </tab>
      </tabs>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: split
components.contract: reads items[] {id, title, age}, detail.{title, status, open, age, summary, owner} (the host keeps detail with a Derive over items and the cursor); reads and writes cur (the cursor row's id)
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap when="#items">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#items">
    <!-- COPY: master / detail is a `row` with class `k-split`: a list on the
         left (`k-split-master`, 34% wide, 24 to 40 columns) and a card on
         the right (`k-split-detail`, the rest). The list `bind` is the
         selected id; the host keeps `detail` (a Derive over `items` and the
         cursor) so the right side follows the cursor with no handler.
         The detail card shows the badge for the status through class:NAME
         guards. -->
    <row class="k-split">
      <list id="items" class="k-menu k-split-master" each="items as it" key="it.id" bind="cur" title="Incidents" on:select="menu_select">
        <item>
          <row class="k-menu-row">
            <text class="k-menu-label">{it.title}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-key">{it.age}</text>
          </row>
        </item>
      </list>
      <box class="k-card k-split-detail" title="{detail.title}">
        <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
          <text class="k-badge" class:danger="detail.open" class:ok="!detail.open">{detail.status}</text>
          <text class="k-muted">{detail.age} ago</text>
        </row>
        <text class="k-card-text" wrap="wrap">{detail.summary}</text>
        <text class="k-card-muted">owner: {detail.owner}</text>
      </box>
    </row>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: hints
components.contract: reads nothing from the store; shows the keymap rows that have a label
components.actions: none of its own (the demo names item_new, item_open, item_next, item_prev, item_search)
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <!-- COPY: every keymap row with a `label` becomes a hint. `keycap` is the
       text shown instead of the key (use it for "j/k" or "^S"). A row
       without a label is bound but not shown. -->
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="n" action="item_new" label="new"/>
    <bind keys="enter" action="item_open" label="open"/>
    <bind keys="j" action="item_next" keycap="j/k" label="move"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="item_prev"/>
    <bind keys="/" action="item_search" label="search"/>
    <bind keys="q" action="quit" label="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col id="app" width="1fr" height="1fr">
      <col width="1fr" height="1fr" pad="1">
        <text class="k-muted">The page content goes here.</text>
      </col>
      <!-- COPY: `<hints/>` with class `k-hints`: one row, the key in the
           accent color (`.hint-key`), the label muted (`.hint-label`; the
           class styles both). Hints that do not fit are dropped from the
           right. `scope="active"` (the default) shows only the keys that
           would fire right now. -->
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: card
components.contract: reads card.title, card.heading, card.text
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#card__open">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">card / panel</text>
      <!-- COPY: a card is a `box` with class `k-card` and a `title`. The
           border turns to the focus color while anything inside holds focus
           (`.k-card:focus-within`). The class gives it `height: auto` to
           wrap its content; write a number or fr on the box to fix it. -->
      <box class="k-card" title="{card.title}">
        <text class="k-card-title">{card.heading}</text>
        <text class="k-card-muted">{card.text}</text>
        <row class="k-card-actions">

          <button id="card__dismiss" class="k-btn ghost" label="Dismiss" on:click="card_dismiss"/>
        </row>
      </box>
      <!-- COPY: side-by-side cards share the row; each takes `1fr`. -->
      <row width="1fr" height="auto" gap="1">
        <box class="k-card" title="Left">
          <text class="k-card-text">First card</text>
        </box>
        <box class="k-card" title="Right">
          <text class="k-card-text">Second card</text>
        </box>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: alert

components.name: badge
components.contract: reads build.number, build.status, build.ok
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <!-- Every kit document loads the sheets in this order: tokens, components, then your own. -->
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">badge</text>
      <!-- COPY: a badge is one text with two classes: `k-badge` and a
           modifier. Modifiers: accent, ok, warn, danger, info (none =
           neutral). The label is literal text or a {path}. -->
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge">draft</text>
        <text class="k-badge accent">new</text>
        <text class="k-badge ok">passing</text>

      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge warn">flaky</text>
        <text class="k-badge danger">failed</text>
        <text class="k-badge info">{build.number}</text>

      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="1">
        <text class="k-badge" class:ok="build.ok" class:danger="!build.ok">{build.status}</text>
      </row>
    </col>

</tui>

components.name: stat
components.contract: reads stats.req.{value, delta, good, hist[]} and stats.err.{value, delta, good, hist[]}
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">stat / KPI card</text>
      <!-- COPY: a stat is a `box` with class `k-stat`: the label as the box
           title, the value in bold, and a row with the change
           (`k-stat-delta`, plus `good` or `bad` for green or red; guard it
           with class:good / class:bad: whether a rise is good depends on
           the metric) and a `sparkline` (class `k-stat-spark`) bound to an
           array of numbers. Put stats in a row; each takes `1fr` of the

      <row width="1fr" height="auto" gap="1">

          <row class="k-stat-row">

            <sparkline class="k-stat-spark" bind="stats.req.hist"/>
          </row>
        </box>
        <box class="k-stat" title="Errors">
          <text class="k-stat-value">{stats.err.value}</text>
          <row class="k-stat-row">
            <text class="k-stat-delta" class:good="stats.err.good" class:bad="!stats.err.good">{stats.err.delta}</text>
            <sparkline class="k-stat-spark" bind="stats.err.hist"/>
          </row>
        </box>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: log
components.contract: reads log.count, log.lines[] {n, text, debug, info, warn, err}; the host appends lines
components.keys: j and k scroll, g top, G follow
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap when="#log">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next" keycap="j/k" label="scroll"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
    <bind keys="G" action="move-last" label="follow"/>
    <bind keys="g" action="move-first" label="top"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#log">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0">
      <!-- COPY: a log panel is a `scroll` with class `k-log` and
           `stick="bottom"`: it follows the end of its content as lines are
           appended, until you scroll up to read; `move-last` (or scrolling
           to the end) makes it follow again. It needs an `id` and must be
           focusable to take the keys. The lines are a `col` with
           `each` and a `key`; `height: auto` (the class) lets the column
           be as tall as its lines, which is what the scroll measures.
           Color a line with class:NAME guards: every line carries all the
           flags (a missing path is B002), `false` for the ones it is not.
           The host appends lines to the array (see examples/kit-gallery). -->
      <scroll id="log" class="k-log" stick="bottom" focusable="true" title="build log · {log.count} lines">
        <col class="k-log-lines" each="log.lines as l" key="l.n">
          <text class="k-log-line" class:muted="l.debug" class:info="l.info" class:warn="l.warn" class:danger="l.err">{l.text}</text>
        </col>
      </scroll>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.keys: j and k move, enter opens

components.name: menu
components.contract: reads menu.items[] {id, icon, label, key}, menu.checked[]; reads and writes menu.cur (the cursor row's id)
components.keys: j and k move, space marks, enter opens
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap when="#menu">
    <bind keys="j" action="move-next"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="move-prev"/>
    <bind keys="space" action="check-toggle" label="mark"/>
    <bind keys="enter" action="menu_open" label="open"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#menu">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">menu / nav list</text>
      <!-- COPY: a menu is a `list` with class `k-menu`; each item is one
           `k-menu-row` (icon, label, shortcut). `bind` holds the cursor
           row's key; `checked` + `mark` add multi-select marks (space
           toggles it through the `check-toggle` built-in). The cursor row is
           bold on a quiet fill while another widget has focus, and a solid
           accent bar while the menu has it. Enter is not implicit in a
           list: bind it to the action that opens the row, as above. -->
      <list id="menu" class="k-menu" each="menu.items as it" key="it.id" bind="menu.cur" checked="menu.checked" mark="✓" title="Go to" on:select="menu_select">
        <item>
          <row class="k-menu-row">
            <text class="k-menu-icon">{it.icon}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-label">{it.label}</text>
            <text class="k-menu-key">{it.key}</text>
          </row>
        </item>
      </list>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: button
components.contract: reads last
components.keys: tab and shift+tab move focus, enter or space presses, q quits
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+c,q" action="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#buttons__primary">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">button</text>
      <text class="k-subtitle">tab / shift+tab moves focus; enter or space presses</text>
      <!-- COPY: a button is `k-btn` plus a modifier: primary, secondary,
           danger, ghost. `on:click` names the action (component_verb); the
           host implements it. The focused button is drawn inverted, bold and
           underlined (see `.k-btn:focus`). -->
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="buttons__primary" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="button_save"/>
        <button id="buttons__secondary" class="k-btn secondary" label="Cancel" on:click="button_cancel"/>
      </row>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="buttons__danger" class="k-btn danger" label="Delete" on:click="button_delete"/>
        <button id="buttons__ghost" class="k-btn ghost" label="Skip" on:click="button_skip"/>
        <button id="buttons__off" class="k-btn secondary" label="Locked" disabled="true"/>
      </row>
      <text class="k-muted">last action: {last}</text>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: field
components.contract: reads and writes forms.profile.{name,email}.value; reads forms.profile.{name,email}.error ("" when fine; the host writes them); the host also writes forms.profile.valid, which the markup does not read
components.keys: ctrl+s saves, enter in an input submits
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+s" action="form_submit" keycap="^S" label="save"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#profile__name">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="0" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">form field</text>
      <!-- COPY: a field is a `col` with class `k-field`: a label, an `input`
           with class `k-field-input`, help text, and an error line. The
           input has its own border (and height 3), which is what lets
           `:focus` change `border-color`; an input without `border` cannot
           show focus that way. The form is named by the id prefix: the
           inputs are `profile__name` and `profile__email`, and the store
           holds `forms.profile.<field>.value` and `.error`. The host writes
           the error ("" when fine): `class:invalid` turns the label and the
           border red, and the error line shows only while the path is
           non-empty. `forms.profile.valid` (true when no rule fails) is the
           host's too; the markup does not need it. -->
      <col class="k-field">
        <text class="k-field-label" class:invalid="forms.profile.name.error">Name</text>
        <input id="profile__name" class="k-field-input" class:invalid="forms.profile.name.error" bind="forms.profile.name.value" placeholder="your name" on:change="form_validate" on:submit="form_submit"/>
        <text class="k-field-help" if="!forms.profile.name.error">Shown on your profile.</text>
        <text class="k-field-error" if="forms.profile.name.error">{forms.profile.name.error}</text>
      </col>
      <col class="k-field">
        <text class="k-field-label" class:invalid="forms.profile.email.error">Email</text>
        <input id="profile__email" class="k-field-input" class:invalid="forms.profile.email.error" bind="forms.profile.email.value" placeholder="you@example.com" on:change="form_validate" on:submit="form_submit"/>
        <text class="k-field-help" if="!forms.profile.email.error">We never share it.</text>
        <text class="k-field-error" if="forms.profile.email.error">{forms.profile.email.error}</text>
      </col>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="profile__save" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="form_submit"/>
        <hints class="k-hints"/>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: confirm
components.contract: reads confirm.open, confirm.title, confirm.message; the host writes confirm.open and confirm.result
components.keys: y confirms, n and esc cancel
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <!-- The overlay's own keys come first: the first matching row in document
       order wins, so they must precede any global row. `when=".k-dialog"`
       holds while focus is anywhere inside a dialog. The host tells the
       instance apart by the prefix of the event's source before the last
       "__" (confirm__yes: the instance is "confirm"). -->
  <keymap when=".k-dialog">
    <bind keys="y" action="dialog_confirm" label="confirm"/>
    <bind keys="n" action="dialog_cancel" label="cancel"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#confirm__open">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">confirm dialog</text>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="confirm__open" class="k-btn danger" label="Delete project" on:click="dialog_open"/>
      </row>
      <text class="k-muted">result: {confirm.result}</text>
    </col>
    <!-- COPY: a confirm dialog is a `modal` with class `k-dialog` (add
         `danger` for a destructive one), the message, and an action row of
         `k-dialog-actions` (height 1). The modal must be the LAST child of
         the screen (L004). `open` is a path the host flips; `focus` puts the
         cursor on the SAFE button, so a stray enter cancels. `on:escape`
         cancels. y / n work too (the keymap above). The class writes the
         modal's size (52 columns, as tall as its content, at most the
         screen). Keep the button labels short: the action row must fit a
         40-column terminal. -->
    <modal id="confirm__dialog" class="k-dialog danger" open="confirm.open" title="{confirm.title}" focus="#confirm__no" on:escape="dialog_cancel">
      <text class="k-dialog-text">{confirm.message}</text>
      <row class="k-dialog-actions">
        <spacer/>
        <button id="confirm__no" class="k-btn secondary" label="Cancel" on:click="dialog_cancel"/>
        <button id="confirm__yes" class="k-btn danger" label="Delete" on:click="dialog_confirm"/>
      </row>
    </modal>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: help
components.contract: reads help.open; lists every keymap row that has a label
components.actions: help_open, help_close (the demo also names item_new, item_delete, item_next, item_prev, item_save)
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <!-- The overlay's own keys come first (the first matching row in document
       order wins), so q and ? close the help instead of reaching the global
       rows below. `when=".k-help"` holds while the help modal is on top. -->
  <keymap when=".k-help">
    <bind keys="q,?" action="help_close" keycap="?" label="close help"/>
  </keymap>
  <!-- COPY: the help overlay lists every keymap row that has a `label`.
       Give rows a `keycap` to show "j/k" or "^S" instead of the raw key. -->
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="?" action="help_open" label="help"/>
    <bind keys="n" action="item_new" label="new item"/>
    <bind keys="d" action="item_delete" label="delete item"/>
    <bind keys="j" action="item_next" keycap="j/k" label="move"/>
    <bind keys="k" action="item_prev"/>
    <bind keys="ctrl+s" action="item_save" keycap="^S" label="save"/>
    <bind keys="q" action="quit" label="quit"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">help overlay</text>
      <text class="k-muted">press ? for the keys</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
    <!-- COPY: a modal with class `k-help` that holds `<hints scope="all">`.
         `scope="all"` lists every labeled row, not only the ones that would
         fire right now. `k-help-keys` stacks them in a column. The class
         writes the modal's size (56 columns, as tall as its content). -->
    <modal id="help__dialog" class="k-help" open="help.open" title="Keys" on:escape="help_close">
      <hints class="k-hints k-help-keys" scope="all"/>
    </modal>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: palette
components.contract: reads palette.commands[], palette.query, found.items[] and found.any (the host keeps found with a Derive over palette.query and palette.commands); reads and writes palette.open, palette.query, palette.cur; reads palette.last
components.actions: palette_open, palette_run, palette_close, palette_query (fires as the query changes; a Go host that filters with Derive needs no work in it, a TypeScript parent recomputes found there)
components.keys: ctrl+k opens, up and down (or ctrl+p and ctrl+n) move, enter runs, esc closes
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <!-- The overlay's own keys come first (the first matching row in document
       order wins). While the palette is open, up / down (and ctrl+n /
       ctrl+p) move the cursor of the list although focus stays in the
       input: the input does not consume them, so they reach the keymap, and
       the built-ins act on the list named by `to`. Enter is the input's
       `on:submit`; esc is the modal's `on:escape`. -->
  <keymap when=".k-palette">
    <bind keys="down,ctrl+n" action="move-next" to="#palette__list"/>
    <bind keys="up,ctrl+p" action="move-prev" to="#palette__list"/>
  </keymap>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="ctrl+k" action="palette_open" keycap="^K" label="commands"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">command palette</text>
      <text class="k-muted">ctrl+k opens it; type, up / down, enter, esc.</text>
      <text class="k-muted">last command: {palette.last}</text>
      <hints class="k-hints"/>
    </col>
    <!-- COPY: a modal with class `k-palette`: an input bound to the query,
         and a list over the filtered commands. The filtering is the HOST's
         job (no expressions in the markup): keep `found` with a Derive over
         `palette.query` and `palette.commands`, so the list always reads the
         result. The list `bind` is the cursor row's id. The class writes the
         modal's size (60 by 16, at most the screen). -->
    <modal id="palette__dialog" class="k-palette" open="palette.open" title="Command palette" focus="#palette__q" on:escape="palette_close">
      <input id="palette__q" class="k-palette-input" bind="palette.query" placeholder="type a command…" on:change="palette_query" on:submit="palette_run"/>
      <text class="k-palette-empty" if="!found.any">No command matches “{palette.query}”.</text>
      <list id="palette__list" class="k-palette-list" each="found.items as r" key="r.id" bind="palette.cur" focusable="false">
        <item>
          <row class="k-palette-row">
            <text class="k-palette-label">{r.label}</text>
            <text class="k-palette-hint">{r.hint}</text>
          </row>
        </item>
      </list>
    </modal>
  </screen>
</tui>

components.name: toast
components.contract: reads toast.show, toast.text, toast.is_ok, toast.is_warn, toast.is_danger; the host clears toast.show after a few seconds
components.source:
<tui theme="auto">
  <style src="../theme.tcss"/>
  <style src="../kit.tcss"/>
  <keymap>
    <bind keys="esc" action="toast_dismiss" label="dismiss"/>
  </keymap>
  <screen id="demo" focus="#toast__show">
    <col width="1fr" height="1fr" gap="1" pad="1">
      <text class="k-title">toast</text>
      <row width="1fr" height="1" gap="2">
        <button id="toast__show" class="k-btn primary" label="Save" on:click="toast_show"/>
      </row>
      <spacer/>
      <!-- COPY: a toast is a one-row strip. `k-toast-slot` is a row that is
           always one row high, so the page never jumps when the toast
           appears; the `k-toast` row inside shows only while `toast.show`
           is true. Info is the default; guard the modifiers `ok`, `warn`,
           `danger` with class:NAME. The HOST clears it: set `toast.show`
           back to false from an `Every` tick (see
           examples/kit-gallery/main.go). The slot is not docked, so it can
           sit above a docked status bar (only one bottom-docked bar per
           container, L005). -->
      <row class="k-toast-slot">
        <row class="k-toast" if="toast.show" class:ok="toast.is_ok" class:warn="toast.is_warn" class:danger="toast.is_danger">
          <text class="k-toast-text">{toast.text}</text>
          <text class="k-toast-key">esc</text>
        </row>
      </row>
    </col>
  </screen>
</tui>
